probe_result: Crash injection across a four-field evidence-renewal write found a conditional failure boundary. With certificate acquisition blocked on a self-consistent renewal record, split persistence remains fail-closed but can lose availability. If restart instead treats a partially renewed field set as current authority and permits reacquisition, crashes after writing only the new epoch, or the new epoch plus start time, can mint certificates that satisfy local epoch/effect/freshness checks while binding to mixed old/new authority. A single atomic versioned renewal record, or immutable generations plus one atomic current-generation pointer, removes this mixed-authority minting window in the tested serialized model.
neuroscience_transfer: Context renewal should have a commit boundary: new evidence must bind to one coherent latent context state, not a hybrid of old and new context fields. Recency plus item identity is insufficient if the authority state that defines those fields is torn.
mechanism_revision: Treat evidence renewal as one authority transition. Gate certificate acquisition on a self-consistent renewal generation; never reacquire against torn renewal fields even when the certificate-level conjunction passes.
scope_guard: Positive claim is limited to a serialized single-writer symbolic model with deterministic effect ids, immutable certificate epoch/effect/observation time, one crash after each renewal field write, and optional reacquisition after restart. No claim for concurrent writers, Byzantine/corrupt storage, nondeterministic effect ids, or transports without an atomic replace/pointer primitive.
